pharm: Hydrophilic bile acid; reduces biliary cholesterol and is choleretic/cytoprotective
quick: Used in ICP; avoid in 1st trimester unless needed
Used in liver disease; avoid in decompensated cirrhosis with care
summary: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA / ursodiol) is a hydrophilic bile acid used for primary biliary cholangitis, dissolution of radiolucent cholesterol gallstones, and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. It reduces biliary cholesterol secretion and protects hepatocytes and bile ducts. It is generally well tolerated.
indications: Dissolution of small radiolucent cholesterol gallstones in functioning gallbladder (non-surgical candidates)
Prevention of gallstones during rapid weight loss
Cholestatic disorders (e.g., cystic fibrosis-associated liver disease, PSC - adjunct)

dosage.d: 13-15 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses (or once daily)
8-12 mg/kg/day, usually as a single bedtime dose or divided
dosage.n: Treat for months; reassess by imaging at 6 months

dosage.d: 300 mg twice daily during weight-loss period
10-15 mg/kg/day (commonly 500 mg BID, up to ~21 mg/kg/day)

admin: Take orally with food to improve absorption and tolerance
For dissolution, ensure a functioning gallbladder and radiolucent (non-calcified) cholesterol stones
Separate dosing from bile-acid sequestrants and antacids by ≥2 hours
Continue long-term in PBC; monitor biochemical response
moa: Replaces and reduces the proportion of hydrophobic, cytotoxic bile acids in the bile acid pool. It decreases hepatic cholesterol synthesis and biliary cholesterol secretion (dissolving cholesterol gallstones), stimulates bile flow (choleresis), and protects hepatocytes and cholangiocytes from bile-acid-induced injury and apoptosis.

absolute: Biliary obstruction (common bile duct/cystic duct occlusion)
Frequent biliary colic / non-functioning gallbladder (for dissolution)
relative: Inflammatory bowel disease with bile acid malabsorption

preg: Commonly used to treat intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy under specialist care with a reassuring safety record; avoid in the first trimester unless clearly needed. Benefits in cholestasis generally outweigh risks.
lact: Limited data; small amounts expected in milk. Generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; use if benefit outweighs risk and monitor the infant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment required in renal impairment; primarily hepatically handled and fecally excreted.
hepatic: Used therapeutically in chronic cholestatic liver disease. Use caution in decompensated cirrhosis; monitor liver function and discontinue if hepatic decompensation worsens.

major: Bile acid sequestrants - cholestyramine, colestipol, colesevelam (bind UDCA, reduce efficacy - separate by ≥2 h)
moderate: Estrogens / oral contraceptives and clofibrate (increase biliary cholesterol, counteract gallstone dissolution)
minor: Ciprofloxacin and dapsone absorption may be affected
interactions.food: Take with food to improve dissolution and bioavailability
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol aggravates underlying liver disease
interactions.diagnostics: Improves cholestatic liver enzymes (ALP, GGT) and bilirubin; serial LFTs assess biochemical response

serious: Worsening of pre-existing liver disease / hepatic decompensation (rare)
Biliary pain / cholecystitis if stones obstruct
emergency: Acute biliary obstruction / cholangitis (severe RUQ pain, fever, jaundice)

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALP, GGT, transaminases, bilirubin) periodically
Biochemical response in PBC (e.g., ALP reduction)
Ultrasound for gallstone size/dissolution at ~6-monthly intervals during dissolution therapy
Symptoms of biliary obstruction or colic
counsel: Take with food, every day, long-term as prescribed
Separate from cholestyramine or antacids by at least 2 hours
Avoid alcohol and discuss other medicines (including the contraceptive pill) with your clinician
Mild loose stools may occur early and usually settle
Report severe right-upper abdominal pain, fever, or yellowing of skin/eyes
Dissolution therapy works slowly and needs follow-up scans
pk: Biochemical improvement over weeks; stone dissolution over months
pearls: First-line and long-term therapy for primary biliary cholangitis; biochemical response predicts prognosis
Only dissolves small, radiolucent cholesterol stones in a functioning gallbladder - not calcified or pigment stones
Recurrence of gallstones is common after stopping dissolution therapy
Separate from bile-acid sequestrants and aluminium antacids to preserve absorption
Effective and well tolerated for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy under specialist care
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double up. Maintain consistent daily dosing for chronic therapy.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely to be serious; the main effect is diarrhea due to bile acid effects in the colon. Manage with supportive care and dose reduction; no specific antidote required.
